title: Investigation: multi-region graceful-degradation oscillation causing repeated SLO slippage
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Between 2026-02-24 03:40 UTC and 2026-02-24 08:10 UTC we observed multiple short-duration SLO breaches (90th and 99th tail) in EU-primary traffic. The control plane routed a portion of EU traffic to the US-west secondary region; subsequent oscillation between regions and a misconfigured circuit breaker hysteresis caused repeated failovers and amplified tail latency for a subset of tenant workloads. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations applied, and the follow-up engineering actions required to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-24 03:40 UTC - first SLO alert (90th latency > 350ms) for eu-prod-route-1.
2026-02-24 03:45 UTC - auto-fallback to us-west triggered by routing policy (latency threshold).
2026-02-24 04:05 UTC - partial recovery seen, traffic re-anchored to EU by sticky-region heuristic.
2026-02-24 04:12 UTC - second spike; circuit breaker opened then half-open quickly due to 30s hysteresis miscalculation.
2026-02-24 04:20-07:00 UTC - repeated short-lived failovers (3-7m windows) between EU <-> US causing KV cache cold starts and tokenized-batching inefficient fill rates.
2026-02-24 07:05 UTC - on-call manually increased hysteresis and pinned critical routes to eu-primary.
2026-02-24 08:10 UTC - system stable, alerts cleared.
metrics_observed: SLOs affected: eu-prod-route-1 90th went from baseline 210ms -> 420ms (peak), 99th spiked from 480ms -> 1.2s. Error budget consumption: ~12% of monthly allowance in a 6-hour window for tiered accounts. Traffic swap rate: ~18% of requests rerouted during oscillation windows. KV cache cold miss ratio increased by 62% during failovers.
root_cause: A combination of three interacting issues: (1) routing policy threshold for automatic fallback was too aggressive relative to short-lived tail noise for eu-prod-route-1; (2) circuit-breaker hysteresis computation used wall-clock values that undercounted active half-open windows when there were frequent open/close transitions, resulting in a 30s hysteresis window that effectively allowed rapid re-openings; (3) sticky-region affinity and cache warmup logic did not account for multi-region cold-start cost when failovers happened repeatedly, causing KV cache misses and poor batching efficiency which amplified latency.
mitigations_taken: Immediately increased fallback latency threshold for eu-prod-route-1 and sibling routes by 40% to reduce sensitivity to tail jitter.
Manually extended circuit-breaker hysteresis to 5 minutes for impacted route group and pinned critical tenant routes to eu-primary for the rest of the incident window.
Applied temporary cache-warmup policy: prefetch top-10 prefixes for pinned tenants on regional reactivation.
Opened high-priority dashboard and mute rules to reduce alert noise while tracking the root-cause metrics.
Notified Sales and Customer Success for high-tier tenants impacted; created customer-level post-incident notes.
Filed a hotfix PR to stop re-evaluating hysteresis windows on every short transition (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13402).
root_cause_analysis_notes: Trade-offs observed: Making the routing threshold less sensitive reduces unnecessary multi-region hops but risks delaying legitimate failovers; increasing hysteresis reduces oscillation but increases time to recover when a real region outage occurs. We concluded the best short-term balance is modestly higher fallbacks plus longer hysteresis for routes with heavy KV cache dependency. Long-term solution will be targeted based on model of workload burstiness per-route.
follow_up_actions: (A) Engineering: Implement deterministic hysteresis state machine that accounts for number of transitions in window and enforces exponential backoff before re-opening (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 3 pts, due: 2026-03-20). Refer to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/resilience/hysteresis-design.

(B) Serving Runtime: Add 'graceful-warmup' hook to replica startup that preloads KV cache for pinned tenants to mitigate cold-start amplification (owner: Mei Tanaka, estimate: 5 pts, due: 2026-04-02).

(C) Platform: Add route-level profile metadata for 'cache-sensitivity' so routing policy can apply conservative heuristics for high-cache routes (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 2 pts, due: 2026-03-31).

(D) Observability: Create a composite SLO dashboard that correlates routing swaps, circuit-breaker state transitions, cache-misses, and batching efficiency; add synthetic canary that simulates 95th+ tail noise (owner: Ruben Castillo, due: 2026-03-12).
(E) Runbooks: Update failover runbook to include detection of oscillation patterns and an automated mitigation to increase hysteresis and pin routes (owner: On-call docs team, due: 2026-03-08).
(F) Governance: Add post-incident customer communication checklist to include SLA risk assessment and credit decisions for impacted tenants (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-05).
(G) Testing: Add chaos test that triggers simulated short tail spikes in EU to validate hysteresis and warmup interplay (owner: SRE, estimate: 3 pts, due: 2026-04-09).
release_notes: Hysteresis deterministic state machine and warmup hook targeted for runtime-2.3.1; route-level cache-sensitivity metadata to be introduced in console-2026.03
